teams.heading: Jake White's Fiji slump to fourth straight defeat, 54-17 to France
teams.body: Fiji coach Jake White's side started with 10 France-based players, including their entire backline, and were typically physical. Their much-vaunted backs struggled to fire. Simione Kuruvoli's penalty was their only reward before the break, when France led 26-3. Selestino Ravutaumada added a second consolation try, while Jiuta Wainiqolo, playing in his adopted home, was unable to make an impact.

lead.why: It is Fiji's own match, and this angle on the defeat has not led an edition yet.

teams.heading: Victor Matfield questions Henry Pollock's hype after his two tries against Australia
teams.body: Former Springboks second row Victor Matfield has questioned the fuss around Henry Pollock on the Rugby Rivals podcast. He cannot see why so much is expected of him. Matfield argued the credit for Pollock's second try, a run to the corner unopposed, belongs to the team-mates who got him the ball. Former All Blacks and Italy coach John Kirwan disagreed, saying England need a superstar and that Pollock is one. Pollock came on at half-time against Australia, moved to the wing and scored twice in two minutes.

lead.why: The Matfield and Kirwan debate over Pollock is the one genuinely new England item, while the other shortlist pieces all restate the Feyi-Waboso and Curry injury news already reported.

teams.heading: Galthié adds Desperes and Le Brun as Jalibert, Ntamack miss Springboks test
teams.body: Fabien Galthié, France head coach, has brought Axel Desperes and Louis Le Brun into preparations for Friday's Springboks test in Paris, widening a fly-half pool stripped by injury. Matthieu Jalibert, Romain Ntamack and Antoine Hastoy are all ruled out, and Thomas Ramos, who has covered No. 10 before, is sidelined too. Reports in France tip Maxime Lucu to start there, but Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus expects a different route: "It will be Lucu or the 13," he said after naming his team.

lead.why: It is the only fresh France team story in the shortlist, covering new call-ups and fly-half absences rather than a profile or pre-match opinion.

teams.heading: Ireland v Fiji and Republic of Ireland's Austria game clash on Saturday
teams.body: Fans have only just clocked the collision: Ireland head coach Andy Farrell's side host Fiji at the Aviva Stadium on Saturday, the same evening the Republic of Ireland football side play Austria in Linz in the Nations League. Caolan's post on X, "That's a pain.", has drawn more than 330 likes, with some fans arguing the schedule should have been different. Ireland beat Argentina 42-12 last Friday, and Fiji are next at the Aviva.

lead.why: It is the only genuinely new item, since the Frawley interview repeats the already-reported news that he is expected to start at out-half.

teams.heading: Tommaso Di Bartolomeo says Italy will target Argentina's scrum and lineout
teams.body: Zebre hooker Tommaso Di Bartolomeo says Italy want to press Argentina on efficiency, ball-winning phases and the scrum and lineout. Speaking after the squad's first day on the grass in Turin, he said the Pumas, beaten 42-12 by Ireland in Dublin, will arrive keen to play their best game. He expects an even contest in which the side bringing more intensity and precision wins, and admitted much could have been done better against South Africa.

lead.why: A new, Italy-side story: hooker Tommaso Di Bartolomeo sets out the plan for the Argentina test, and the Argentina call-up item is Argentina's story.

teams.heading: Harry Wilson's Wallabies lose 45-22 at Twickenham, a fairer fight for Scotland
teams.body: Wallabies captain Harry Wilson said at full-time: "We've got seven days to take some feedback from this game and make sure we're a lot better because Scotland are a really good team." Planet Rugby's opinion column reads Australia's problems as deeper than one result, citing porous defence, a revolving cast at fly-half and poor control of possession under new coach Les Kiss. It sees Scotland as a closer test than England was, which could make for an even contest.

teams.heading: WRU cuts student tickets for Wales v All Blacks to £20
teams.body: A flash sale that went live on Tuesday, four days before Saturday's Wales v New Zealand match at the Principality Stadium, cuts student tickets to £20. Upper-tier student seats, priced at £62.50, have been cut by more than 63%, and Category B seats near the halfway line, £98 for adults, are part of the £20 offer. The WRU is trying to boost the crowd: last weekend's Japan match drew 52,425, against 61,324 a year earlier, after the union recently posted annual losses of £18m.

lead.why: A fresh WRU ticket move affecting Saturday's Wales match, not already covered in this tab's editions.

teams.heading: Hooper, Gordon and Paenga-Amosa set to be fit for Scotland
teams.body: Three players who missed the England defeat are in contention for the Scotland test. Tom Hooper's shoulder problem was re-aggravated with Exeter last month. Flyhalf Carter Gordon is still returning from the broken leg he suffered against Argentina in September, while hooker Brandon Paenga-Amosa has had knee bruising from the Sydney training camp. Scrum coach John Ulugia said: "Everyone's on deck." The side is due to be named on Friday.

lead.why: A new team-news item on three returning players ahead of the Scotland test, and the Bell card has already been reported today.

teams.heading: Jason Ryan asks World Rugby to consider maul law change
teams.body: All Blacks forwards coach Jason Ryan has called on World Rugby to consider a law change at the maul, which produced three first-half tries in last Saturday's 43-21 win over Scotland. Peter Lakai scored from a 20th-minute maul, but Scotland scored twice as extra players joined their drives, and Ryan said: "They add their backs in and next minute it's a 12 on eight." Ryan also said the review had focused on accuracy and decision-making, and that back-to-back double yellow cards had put the defence under pressure.

lead.why: It is a new item in which the All Blacks' own coach makes a specific call on the laws, and it is not a repeat of the Jordan and Barrett news already reported.

teams.heading: Morne van den Berg starts at scrum-half against France, Reinach on bench
teams.body: Erasmus has kept faith with the man who started against Italy, judging it best for the Springboks that Cobus Reinach is held in reserve. Van den Berg, a 12-cap Springbok aged 29, now faces France scrum-half Antoine Dupont, the 65-cap player many consider the best in the world at nine. Retired prop Steven Kitshoff, speaking on For the Love of Rugby South Africa, said: "The way that Morne is currently playing, he has got a lot of Dupont in him."

lead.why: It is the one new team-selection fact in the pack, the Springboks' scrum-half choice against France, and the Jeremy Ward story has already run today.
